name: Museo de Arte de El Salvador (MARTE)
watch: Sponsor wall lists Avanza Consultores, The Zemurray Foundation, C. Imberton, Alas Doradas, Viva Outdoor, AR and Ternova.
records_note: No annual reports or accounts found; six sponsor logos with no names are shown undated, and the board list names only its president.

name: Museo de Arte de Ponce
funding: Founders Ferré-Rangel and Fonalledas families and Fundación Ángel Ramos; 700+ individuals; corporate gala sponsors led by Banco Popular.
watch: Fossil money on its own sponsors page: Puma Energy, New Fortress Energy, plus UBS. The list is from the 2019 gala.
records_note: Posts annual reports for 2022-23 and 2023-24 and a named sponsor list with 2019 gala tiers; no accounts on its site, but the operating foundation's Form 990 is public.

name: Museo de Arte de Zapopan
watch: Free public contemporary art museum. The old domain mazmuseo.com now carries casino spam links; the municipal site is maz.zapopan.gob.mx.
records_note: The municipal museum's site lists exhibitions, programmes and a contact address, with no annual reports, accounts, sponsor names or board.

name: Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires (MALBA)
funding: Fundación Costantini, ICBC, Citi, corporate circles.
watch: Private foundation museum with banking and multinational sponsorships.
why_flagged: Fundación Malba, set up by Eduardo Costantini, runs it. Its 2024 audited accounts show founder gifts at 12 percent of income, presenting partners and sponsors 58 percent and own earnings 17 percent, with a surplus. Collaborators on its sponsors page include Chevron, Bloomberg, Zurich and Telecom.
records_note: It posts financial statements for 2005 to 2024 but no annual report; sponsors show only as logos and no board members are named.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM)
funding: Mid-size private museum founded 1978; pillars are Medellín city hall, national Culture Ministry, Comfama, SURA, Bancolombia, EPM, Fundación Fraternidad and Fundación MUV.
watch: Public utility EPM is a pillar; Celsia (an energy firm) is credited for website support.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports for 2022 to 2025, 2024 financial statements, a named list of pillars and allies, and its 12-member board.

name: Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo
funding: Agency of Costa Rica's Ministry of Culture, paid through the national budget. Budget pages are online for 2013 to 2020.
watch: The complex belongs to the Centro Nacional de Cultura.
records_note: A ministry agency: posts management reports from 1992 to 2022, financial statements for 2013 to 2019 and budgets to 2020; no funder list or board.

name: Museo de la Ciudad de México
funding: Public museum run by the Mexico City Ministry of Culture.
watch: A federal judge suspended Fabián Cháirez's show in April 2025 after an amparo suit. The city culture ministry defended the show.
records_note: The museum's site and its Culture Secretariat's site did not connect, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Museo de los Pintores Oaxaqueños
funding: State museum run by the Oaxaca state patronato for cultural and tourist units.
watch: Temporary exhibitions only, no permanent collection. The state government began rehabilitating the colonial building. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: The museum is run by Oaxaca's state cultural patronage board, whose sites did not connect, so reports, accounts, funders and board are unchecked.

name: Museo del Barro
funding: Private foundation museum (Escobar, Salerno); 2026 sponsors page names Banco Itaú, Citibank, French embassy, a law firm and named friends.
watch: Bank money named: Itaú (sponsor) and Citibank (supporter).
records_note: Its sponsors page names a bank sponsor, supporters and named friends, but the site posts no annual reports, accounts or foundation board.

name: Museo del Prado
funding: 3.5M visitors (2025). Benefactors Fundación BBVA (2025) and Fundación AXA (2024); Fundación Iberdrola España funds fellowships to 2027; Fundación Endesa, Rassini and la Caixa (to 2025) fund projects.
watch: Utilities Iberdrola (66% renewable capacity) and Endesa fund programmes; both sell gas. la Caixa's holding Criteria owns 28.5% of gas utility Naturgy.
records_note: Its site answers every request with a Cloudflare check, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be read; only BOE funder agreements were opened.

name: Museo Experimental El Eco
watch: Entrepreneur Daniel Mont paid for the 1953 building by Mathias Goeritz. UNAM bought and reopened it in 2005. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: El Eco has no records of its own; owner UNAM posts audited annual accounts for 2022 to 2025 and names its governing boards.

name: Museo Ixchel del Traje Indígena
funding: Small private textile museum on the UFM campus; paid for by membership tiers (Q300 to Q10,000), the US charity Friends of the Ixchel Museum (since 1984) and project grants.
watch: Its 'current members' sponsor page names nobody. Past conservation grants came from Getty, Finland, the Carene Foundation and the US Embassy.
records_note: The museum publishes no reports, accounts, named donors or board; only its US friends charity files Form 990-EZ, 2009 to 2025.
